P1Q1.q: According to Aquinas, why is sacred doctrine necessary in addition to philosophical science?
options: Because philosophy is unreliable and often wrong
Because man is directed to an end (salvation) that exceeds what reason can grasp
Because philosophers disagree with one another
Because sacred doctrine replaces the need for reason entirely
P1Q1.explanation: Aquinas argues that since man is ordained to an end (eternal life) beyond what reason can conceive, it was necessary that things beyond reason be made known through divine revelation.

P1Q1.q: Is sacred doctrine, in Aquinas's view, one science or many?
options: Many sciences, one for each article of faith
One science, because it considers things under the formality of being divinely revealed
Not a science at all, only opinion
P1Q1.explanation: Aquinas holds sacred doctrine is one science because unity of a science depends on the unity of its formal object — here, things as divinely revealed.

P1Q1.q: What does Aquinas say about sacred doctrine's use of philosophical arguments from authority?
options: It relies wholly and only on the authority of philosophers
It uses philosophical arguments as the weakest kind of proof, subordinate to the authority of Scripture
It forbids the use of philosophy
It treats philosophers as equal in authority to canonical Scripture
P1Q1.explanation: Sacred doctrine properly argues from the articles of faith; arguments from human reason or philosophers are used only to illustrate, and are the weakest form of proof, since Scripture's authority is what truly grounds the science.
